Review completed with 2 findings across 2 agents (2 high).

⚠️ 2 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [HIGH] Password Hash Disclosure Due to Strict Model Equality Check (SecurityAgent)
  - [HIGH] Logic error: MTI user models reveal password hash (LogicAgent)

findings.title: Password Hash Disclosure Due to Strict Model Equality Check
findings.description: The check `field.model == get_user_model()` introduces a regression in data exposure. Previously, any model inheriting from `AbstractBaseUser` or matching `AUTH_USER_MODEL` would have its password hashed. Now, only the exact `AUTH_USER_MODEL` class is masked. If `AUTH_USER_MODEL` is a child model in a multi-table inheritance hierarchy (e.g., `ChildUser` inheriting from `ParentUser` which has the `password` field), `field.model` will be `ParentUser`. Since `ParentUser != ChildUser`, the check fails, and the raw password hash is displayed instead of the masked version. This exposes sensitive cryptographic material (password hashes) to admin users with view-only permissions on the specific model, violating confidentiality.

findings.title: Logic error: MTI user models reveal password hash
findings.description: The new condition fails to handle multi-table inheritance (MTI) where the `password` field is defined on a parent model (e.g., `AbstractBaseUser`), but the admin instance or `AUTH_USER_MODEL` is a concrete child model. In such cases, `field.model` will be the parent, while `get_user_model()` returns the child, causing the equality check to fail. This leads to the password hash being rendered as a plain value instead of a secure hashed representation.
findings.suggestion: Restore the inheritance check: `if field.name == "password" and (issubclass(field.model, AbstractBaseUser) or issubclass(get_user_model(), field.model)):`
